newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended a directionless Tuesday slightly down, but well off the day's lows as market eyes searched in vain for guidance, dealers said.
After Monday's Wall Street-inspired heady gains some market figures were prepared for another strong day as the Dow set another record high overnight.

But the scale of the New York rise -- a mere 5.39 points -- meant little positive sentiment was added and mild profit-taking entered the South African market. Dealers said there was little else to guide the market.
"It has been a relatively quiet day. Wall Street had little effect on us," said one dealer.

The market also shrugged off news of a diplomatic spat between South Africa and the United States over planned arms sales by Pretoria to Syria. The news did not hit shares, but for a while impacted on the bond market.

The all-share index dropped 6.7 points to 6,751.9 as the industrial index fell 4.9 points to 8,125.8. Dealers said there was a healthy turnover of about 574 million rands worth of shares with demand coming from local institutions and overseas.
But dealers said demand was more selective than during Monday's impressive rally.

As a result blue-chip firms posted mixed performances with Anglos off 250 cents to 257.50 rand and JCI down 10 cents to 43.90 rand while Richemont ended up 50 cents to 66 rand and Minorco put on 25 cents to 103 rand.

The one real feature of the day was the performance of information technology stock Persetel which shed eight percent, or 350 cents, to 34.00 rand following the group's announcement of a major German buy.

Dealers and analysts said the drop was largely due to the dilutive effect of Persetel's plans to fund the acquisition by issuing 70 million new shares -- a massive dilution of its existing 186 million share capital.
There are also some worries in the market over the size of the confidential price-tag for Telemation.
Gold shares dipped down again on bullion woes, but dealers said the sector held up well and reported a mild renewal of interest in the index.
"There were some buyers out there, which has been rare recently," one dealer said.

The golds index lost 10.3 points to 1,449.9 as Kloof shed 25 cents to 36.25 rand and Vaal Reefs lost 150 cents 298.50 rand. Western Deeps reversed the trend to put on 50 cents to finish at 132.00 rand.
Dealers said the South African share market was probably set for another drifting day on Wednesday, unless there were major gains on Wall Street overnight.
"A big rise will be a positive influence, but another small gain will see a similar pattern to today," one dealer said.
